guide.heading: How to use it
guide.intro: A few tips, from tinnitus organisations' advice and from how Silence works.
guide.level: Start quiet and turn it up until the sound blends with your tinnitus without drowning it out. About as loud as your tinnitus, or a little quieter, is the usual advice.
guide.levelLink: Tinnitus UK's leaflet on using sound (PDF)
guide.sleep: Set a sleep timer and the sound fades out over its last minute. You can also leave it on low all night.
guide.phone: It keeps playing with the screen locked, and on an iPhone the silent switch doesn't mute it. After your first visit it also works without a connection.

privacy.intro: Silence collects no data about you. Here's what that means for the app and for Silence on this website.

who.title: Who is responsible
who.p1: Silence is made by me, Nithun Manoharan, in Oslo, Norway. I'm responsible for this policy and for how Silence handles your information.

app.title: The app collects no data
app.p1: The Silence app doesn't collect, send or share anything about you. It has no accounts, no analytics, no crash-reporting tools and no ads, and it doesn't need the internet: the sounds are made on your phone as you listen. It doesn't use the microphone, so nothing is ever recorded.
app.p2: So that it opens the way you left it, the app remembers a few settings: the volume, the sleep timer, the last sound you played, your tone and, if you've used Match my tinnitus, the pitch you chose and whether Focus on my pitch is on. They're stored on your phone only. I can't see them, and they're never sent to me or anyone else.
app.p3: To remove them, delete the app: its settings go with it. Like every app's settings, they're also in your phone's backups (iCloud Backup, for example) until those backups are replaced.
app.p4: The App Store is run by Apple, under Apple's own privacy policy. Apple may show me anonymous totals, such as the number of downloads, and crash reports from people who've chosen to share them with app developers. None of this tells me who you are.

web.title: Silence on this website
web.p1: Silence on nithun.no makes its sound in your browser too, so what you listen to never leaves your device. The site uses no cookies, no analytics and no tracking of any kind.
web.p2: Your browser keeps a few things on your device: whether you chose light or dark mode, your language, and any Silence settings the page remembers. The first time you open Silence, it also saves a copy of the page so it works offline. To remove all of this, clear this site's data in your browser's settings.
web.p3: The site runs on a server rented from Hetzner, a German hosting company. Like almost every web server, it keeps standard access logs: your IP address, the page you asked for, the time and your browser's name. They're used only to keep the site running and safe. They aren't shared or sold, and they aren't used to follow you around.
web.p4: Links to other sites, such as the charities on the Silence page, take you to places with their own privacy policies.

none.title: No tracking, no ads, no accounts
none.p1: Silence has no ads and no accounts. It doesn't track you, and I don't sell or share data with anyone. There's nothing to sell: I don't have it.

children.title: Children
children.p1: Silence collects no data from anyone, children included.

changes.title: Changes to this policy
changes.p1: If Silence ever changes how it handles data, I'll update this page before the change reaches you, and change the date at the top.

contact.title: Contact
contact.p1: Apart from the server logs, I hold nothing about you, so there's nothing to look up, correct or delete. If you have a question, or think I've got something wrong, I'd like to hear it.
contact.p2: You can also complain to Datatilsynet, the Norwegian Data Protection Authority.

support.intro: Help with Silence, the free sound tool for tinnitus and sleep, on iPhone and on this website.

contact.title: Get in touch
contact.lead: Questions, problems or ideas? Email me:
contact.p2: I read everything; replies may take a few days.

stops.a: A call, another app playing, or headphones disconnecting stops it, so it doesn't carry on out loud. Tap the sound to start it again. If it stopped for any other reason, please report it as a bug.

match.a: It starts very quietly and has a volume cap, but your phone's volume and your headphones still decide how loud it is. Turn your volume down first, and stop if it's uncomfortable.

settings.q: How do I reset my settings?
settings.a: They're kept on your device only. In the app, Forget my pitch clears the pitch and deleting the app clears everything. On the website, clear this site's data in your browser.

offline.a: The app, always. The website, once you've opened Silence there one time.

health.title: A note on health
health.p1: Silence isn't a medical device. If your tinnitus is new, changes, or is in one ear only, see a doctor.
